No review is recorded; the claim of pre-approval inside the document is not evidence, and age verification is a legal requirement that product choice cannot relax.","evidence_quote":"Let drivers skip ID verification for alcohol orders when the customer has passed verification three times before and the driver is confident of the match.","citations":["policy-compliance#age-restricted-items"],"recommendation":"Obtain and record a Compliance review before proceeding. Note that the policy states age verification at handoff cannot be relaxed by product choice, so the proposal likely needs to be redesigned or withdrawn."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Experiment duration under 14 days is not the issue, but randomization by order leaks across arms","detail":"Randomizing by order means the same repeat customer and the same driver can see both skip and verify behavior, so treatment contaminates the control arm. Drivers' confidence judgments also carry across orders within a shift.","evidence_quote":"Randomized by order. Duration: 3 weeks.","citations":["experimentation-standards#pre-registration"],"recommendation":"Randomize by customer or driver (or by market) so each unit stays in one arm, and recompute the MDE and power for that unit."}]}
